run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T18:07:52Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by 504s the proxy itself emits on POST /api/checkout: Envoy tags them 504 UT response_timeout with a 15000 ms duration, because the checkout flow behind frontend takes ~30 s. Inside checkout the only slow hop is its HTTP client call to the email Service: the PlaceOrder server span lasts ~30.4 s while every other downstream call (cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping, payment, kafka 'orders publish') completes in milliseconds, and the checkout pod logs 'failed POST to email service: Post "http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation": dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' where 100.67.49.77 is the email Service ClusterIP. The email Service has two running, ready, never-restarted endpoints that keep answering other requests in 3-4 ms with HTTP 200 and show no error spans, so the email application is not failing; TCP connections to the email Service address intermittently blackhole (~101 thirty-second dial timeouts in 78 minutes, with the 5-minute ingress error rate rising from 0-0.015/s before ~18:08 to 0.2-0.35/s from 18:10). The exact network element that drops the SYN/SYN-ACK handshake (kube-proxy/endpoint forwarding on the client side vs one email endpoint's network stack) cannot be identified from the available data.

claims.text: Over the 78-minute window 17:07:52-18:25:52, frontend-proxy span 'ingress' increased by 220.9 spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR versus 19031.9 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET; span 'router frontend egress' increased by 0 error spans.

The 5-minute rate of frontend-proxy 'ingress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans was 0.008-0.015/s in samples from 17:50:52 to 18:08:52 and 0/s in several of them, then rose to 0.2 at 18:10:52, 0.3519 at 18:12:52, 0.2963, 0.3400, 0.2914 and 0.1031 at 18:22:52; the 10-minute rate went from 0.00556 at 18:06:02 to 0.28246 at 18:16:02.

The sampled frontend-proxy error spans are all operation 'ingress' with error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR and durations of ~15,000,000 microseconds (e.g. 15001496, 15001318, 15000610 us).

The frontend-proxy access log records the failures as upstream timeouts on the checkout route, e.g. '"POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout - "-" 382 24 15000', with 267 lines matching '504' between 18:05 and 18:26.

In trace 4824dfdd47ada84d818501ec6a6f3c0f the frontend server span 'POST /api/checkout' lasted 30.42 s and returned http.status_code 200, the frontend gRPC client span 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' lasted 30.42 s, the checkout server span 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' lasted 30.42 s with rpc.grpc.status_code 0, the checkout client span 'HTTP POST' lasted 30.0 s with error=true and otel.status_description 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout', the checkout 'orders publish' span ran at +30.4 s (216 us), and the frontend-proxy 'ingress' span for the same request was a 15.0 s 504.

A 25-row slice of checkout error spans shows three 'HTTP POST' spans of 30,000,762 / 30,000,225 / 30,000,210 us each carrying otel.status_description 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout', each inside a checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' span of ~30.0-30.1 s whose own rpc.grpc.status_code is 0.

The only checkout span name with errors in the window is 'HTTP POST' (increase 100.9); per-service error-span increases are frontend-proxy 220.9, checkout 100.9, recommendation 3.05, ad 2.04, fraud-detection 2.04 and 0 for accounting, frontend and payment.

Checkout's 'HTTP POST' spans exceeded 15 s 191.5 times (3046.5 spans at le=+Inf vs 2855.0 at le=15000.0) and its 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' spans exceeded 15 s 201.6 times (1018.2 vs 816.6) in the window, while its internal downstream calls stayed fast.
Service 'email' in otel-demo has clusterIP 100.67.49.77 and one port 8080/TCP with targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=email.

The email Service has two ready endpoints: 100.96.2.7 (pod email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn) and 100.96.3.218 (pod email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w); both pods are Running, Ready=True with restartCount 0, started 2026-11-16T17:34:36Z and owned by ReplicaSet email-59f69bc6cf.

Email's own server spans show 908 'POST /send_order_confirmation' spans in the window, all STATUS_CODE_UNSET with no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series, and sampled email spans complete in 3,942-4,169 us with http.status_code 200 (send_email and sinatra.render_template a few hundred us).
Both email pods kept receiving 'POST /send_order_confirmation' traffic during the incident window (5-minute rates per exported_instance, e.g. 3fb61602-... 0.092 and 6a3edbee-... 0.146 at 18:22:52).

Spans longer than 15 s in the window exist only for frontend (767.5), frontend-proxy (315.6), checkout (393.2), accounting (10.2), ad (2.0), fraud-detection (2.0) and recommendation (3.1); the count is 0 for email, cart, currency, payment, product-catalog, quote, shipping and image-provider.

The checkout container log states 'failed to send order confirmation to "tobias@example.com": failed POST to email service: Post "http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation": dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' and immediately continues with 'sending to postProcessor' and 'order placed', i.e. the email failure is logged and skipped but costs the request ~30 s.

All 22 otel-demo pods are Running with restartCount 0, all were created at 17:34:2x-3x (environment start, not a rollout inside the incident), and all 5 cluster nodes report Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable all False.

The alert mechanism is: checkout's HTTP client cannot open a TCP connection to the email Service ClusterIP 100.67.49.77:8080, Go's dial timeout expires after 30 s, PlaceOrder therefore completes at ~30.4 s, the frontend /api/checkout call exceeds frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream timeout, Envoy returns 504 UT response_timeout, and those ingress error spans raise RequestErrorRate for frontend-proxy.

The 30 s connect timeouts are caused by dropped SYN/SYN-ACK on the network path to the email Service address rather than by the email application: the only direct evidence is the client-side 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' error plus the fact that email's server spans stay in the millisecond range with 200 responses; the data cannot say whether kube-proxy/iptables forwarding on the checkout node or an email endpoint's network stack is responsible.

A second, still-open possibility is that one of the two email endpoints (100.96.2.7 or 100.96.3.218) intermittently blackholes new connections while the other serves normally; this fits the partial failure share with both pods still receiving traffic, but the failing dials carry no pod identity, so the affected endpoint cannot be named.

The email application itself shows no fault: its server spans never exceeded 15 s, it returned 908 order-confirmation requests with 200 in 3-4 ms, both pods are Ready with restartCount 0, and both kept serving during the incident, so an email OOM/crash/restart or email-side slowness is not what the evidence shows.

In trace 4bc2b254d8a95ff609cbb64bb843f53b the email service answered POST /send_order_confirmation with 200 in 4,017 us, yet the same request's frontend POST span lasted 15.18 s and the ingress ended as a 15.0 s 504, so connectivity to email is intermittent and not uniformly broken, and some multi-second stalls on the checkout path are not fully attributable from this trace alone (the checkout PlaceOrder span is absent there).

Checkout's other HTTP and gRPC calls are healthy in the very same slow traces (shipping /get-quote 2,503 us, /ship-order 558 us, cart GetCart 758 us, payment Charge 443 us, currency Convert 1,657 us), which argues against general CPU or network saturation of the checkout pod or of node i-071e7666000f6d243 and localises the fault to the email hop.

A frontend-proxy defect was considered and rejected: its 504 ingress spans are tagged response_flag 'UT response_timeout' after exactly 15,000 ms while the upstream frontend was still working and only returned at ~30.4 s, i.e. the proxy is enforcing its own timeout on a genuinely slow upstream request.

An email pod eviction, OOM kill or crash loop was considered and rejected: both email pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and no previous container instance, and their spans show normal 200 responses during the incident.

Capture the network layer for the email hop: kube-proxy/IPVS rules and conntrack table state on node i-071e7666000f6d243 (where checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs runs), plus repeated TCP connects from the checkout pod to 100.67.49.77:8080 and to each pod IP 100.96.2.7:8080 / 100.96.3.218:8080, to identify which element drops the handshake.

Align timeouts so a slow email call cannot surface as proxy 504s: checkout's email POST has an effective ~30 s dial timeout while frontend-proxy aborts /api/checkout at 15 s, so shortening the email client timeout (or making the confirmation call non-blocking) would remove the 504s even while the connectivity problem persists.

gaps: Logs for the email pods (email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w, email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn) and for frontend-675fd7b5c5-kzdpp returned zero bytes (status no_data), so no application-side log evidence exists for those pods.

No node-level network telemetry is registered: queries for node_nf_conntrack*, node_sockstat* and node_netstat* returned no metric names, so conntrack exhaustion or socket pressure on node i-071e7666000f6d243 could not be checked.
The NetworkPolicy query for otel-demo returned no_data with 0 items, so the absence of a policy blocking checkout->email is not established.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so what changed around 18:05-18:10 (the onset seen in the 5-minute error rate) is unknown.
The email Service sessionAffinity value was redacted in the returned spec, so client-IP affinity could not be verified or ruled out.
Which email endpoint (pod) dropped the failing connections is unknown: the checkout error spans and log lines carry only the ClusterIP 100.67.49.77, not a pod identity.
Prometheus history for these series starts around 17:56-18:09, so a longer pre-incident baseline than the 17:50-18:08 low-error period is unavailable.
The kafka service returned no traces_span_metrics_calls_total series in the window, so its health is unknown (it is not implicated by any observed error).

The alert rule itself could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data both for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for type alert, so the exact alert expression behind the reported 0.2444 value is unverified (the proxy's own ingress error ratio in the sampled slice is consistent with it).
Small error-span increases for ad (2.04), fraud-detection (2.04) and recommendation (3.05) and 10.2 spans over 15 s in accounting were not investigated and are not tied to this alert.

Several views used for the slow-trace analysis were incomplete or truncated slices (9b014906-...-t0, b14ed517-...-t0, 26d3f47f-...-t0, 53a38eba-...-t1, 9df017de-...-t0, 9a44cafc-...-t0), so the counts quoted describe the rows shown, not a complete population.
next_steps: Inspect kube-proxy/IPVS and conntrack state on node i-071e7666000f6d243 and run repeated TCP connects from checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs to 100.67.49.77:8080, 100.96.2.7:8080 and 100.96.3.218:8080 to find which hop drops the handshake.

Review the checkout deployment's email client timeout (currently an effective ~30 s dial timeout) against frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream timeout, and consider making the order-confirmation call asynchronous.
Enable the change_history integration and check for any change to the email Service/Deployment or node networking shortly before 18:05.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition from the Alertmanager/Prometheus rule source to confirm the metric and denominator behind the 0.2444 reading.
Track frontend-proxy ingress 504 rate and checkout 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080' log lines after any fix to confirm the alert clears.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.
